records.name: Rotary Club of Philadelphia
records.summary: A Rotary club of business and professional members, part of Rotary District 7450. It focuses its service on people in need, mostly in Philadelphia and some abroad.
records.what_you_do: Come to an evening meeting with a speaker, sign up for a service day such as the Mount Moriah Cemetery cleanup, or join a fundraising walk team.

schedule.text: Evening meetings at 6 pm on the dates the club lists (Oct 1 and Nov 5, 2026). The page does not publish a regular meeting day.

locations.label: Pyramid Club (venue for the Nov 5, 2026 meeting)

cost.text: Guest policy and dues are not published. Some events cost money, such as a block of $99 tickets for a Dec 6, 2026 concert.

first_step.how: Register for the next meeting or a volunteer day on the club's page, ask to speak at a meeting through the page's form, or use the membership form
first_step.basis: Public events are posted with registration links and visitors can ask to speak, but the club does not publish a guest policy.

records.notes: Read from the club's own page, which lists an Oct 1, 2026 meeting, an Oct 10, 2026 cemetery cleanup and a Nov 5, 2026 meeting. The club's mailing address names a staff member, so it is left out. Rotary's national club finder returned 429 on every try, so no other Philadelphia Rotary club was confirmed here. Chestnut Hill Rotary is named on this page (see leads_only).

records.name: Philadelphia-Kinship Care & Seniors Support Network (Optimist Club 02362)
records.summary: An Optimist club based in Philadelphia, named for kinship care and support for seniors. The national directory lists a noon meeting at Greater Harrison Community Center, but shows no recent news.
records.what_you_do: Ask about the club through its inquiry form on the Optimist directory page, then attend a meeting if the club is still running.

schedule.text: Meeting time is listed as variable, at noon

locations.label: Greater Harrison Community Center
locations.address: Thompson and 10th Street (as listed; no street number given)

first_step.how: Send a question through the club's online inquiry form (linked from the Optimist directory page)
first_step.basis: The only way in that is listed is an inquiry form, and the meeting schedule is listed as variable, so what a visit is like is unclear.

records.notes: Only the national Optimist directory was checked. The listing shows a charter date of Dec 29, 2005 and no news, event or meeting notice, so status is unknown (a charter date is not a sign of activity). No club website or contact email is published. Sponsored by Lower Montco and World Peace Plus-Philadelphia (both leads_only).

records.name: Galilee Community Optimist Club (Optimist Club 02773)
records.summary: An Optimist club that the national directory lists under Philadelphia, but its meeting place is in Ambler, in Montgomery County. The listing does not say it serves city residents.

schedule.text: 2nd Monday of each month at 7 pm, as listed

records.notes: Hidden from results as out of area. Revisit only if the club says it serves Philadelphia residents. The listing shows a charter date of May 5, 2014 and no dated news. Sponsored by Lower Montco and Media-Rose Tree.

records.name: Philadelphia's First Toastmasters Club
records.summary: A public speaking club chartered in 1947 that meets on Zoom to practice speeches and give each other feedback. Visitors can come for free and do not have to speak until they feel ready.
records.what_you_do: Give short prepared speeches when you are ready, and take meeting roles such as timer or evaluator.

schedule.text: 1st and 3rd Thursdays, 7 to 9 pm, on Zoom

cost.text: Club visits are free. Dues are not shown.

first_step.how: Visit a meeting on Zoom for free, using the club's visit form or by calling the listed number
first_step.basis: The club says visits are free, guests do not have to speak until ready, and anyone can join with no membership requirements.

records.notes: The club's own site lists a virtual meeting on Sept 3, 2026 and upcoming meetings on Oct 15, Nov 5 and Nov 19, 2026. Chartered Nov 1, 1947. The club's site notes an uncertain time zone on one notice, which does not change the listed 7 pm start.

records.name: SEPTA Toastmasters
records.summary: A Toastmasters club that meets at lunchtime at SEPTA headquarters on Market Street, in person or online, to practice public speaking. Visits are free, and guests do not have to speak until they are ready.
records.what_you_do: Practice short speeches at lunchtime meetings, and take meeting roles such as timer or evaluator.

schedule.text: 2nd and 4th Wednesdays at noon, except December

cost.text: Club visits are free. Dues are not shown.

first_step.how: Call the listed number or use the club's visit form, then come to a lunchtime meeting in person or online
first_step.basis: The listing says visits are free and guests need not speak until ready, and the club says anyone may join.

records.notes: The club's own site has no dated items and says its schedule is coming soon, but it gives the 2nd and 4th Wednesday schedule. The listing says anyone may join, but the club meets inside a SEPTA office building, so ask before visiting whether people who do not work at SEPTA are welcome. Chartered Oct 16, 2013.

records.name: Northeast Philly Toastmasters
records.summary: An online Toastmasters club for practicing public speaking. The national listing shows Tuesday evening meetings, but the club's own page says its schedule is still being posted.

schedule.text: Tuesdays at 7 pm, online, according to the national listing. The club's own page says its schedule is coming soon.

cost.text: Club visits are free. Dues are not shown.

first_step.how: RSVP through the club's Meetup page to get the Zoom link, or use the club's visit form
first_step.basis: The listing says visits are free and guests need not speak until ready, and the club gives a clear way to RSVP.

records.notes: The club's own site has no dated items. Its visitor counter (since 2025-08-31) is not evidence of meetings. Charter date July 1, 2010. The Zoom link is only shared after RSVP. Meetup is a lead platform, so the Meetup page itself was not read.

records.name: Dr. Constance E. Clayton Education Center (Toastmasters club 28678420)
records.summary: A Toastmasters club that meets at midday at the Dr. Constance E. Clayton Education Center on North Broad Street, a School District of Philadelphia building. Visits are free, but the listing says membership may have professional or educational requirements.

cost.text: Club visits are free. Dues are not shown.

first_step.how: Call the listed number or use the club's visit form before coming
first_step.basis: Visits are free and the club welcomes guests, but membership may have professional or educational prerequisites, so the way in is less clear.

records.notes: Only the national Toastmasters listing was checked. The club's sole dated item is its charter date (Feb 1, 2025), so status is unknown. The prerequisites line is the club's own wording: 'may have professional and/or educational prerequisites', so it is not confirmed for every member.

records.name: Sub & Surface Club (Toastmasters club 00002886)
records.summary: A Toastmasters club that meets at noon at the Navy Yard in South Philadelphia, in person or online, to practice public speaking. Visits are free, and guests do not have to speak until they feel ready.
records.what_you_do: Practice short speeches at lunchtime meetings, and take meeting roles such as timer or evaluator.

locations.label: The Navy Yard (entrance at the leasing office, reached from Chapel Way)

cost.text: Club visits are free. Dues are not shown.

first_step.how: Call the listed number or use the club's contact form, then come in person or join online
first_step.basis: The listing says visits are free, guests need not speak until ready, and anyone may join.

records.notes: The club's own site loads and gives the schedule and both in-person and online options, but has no dated items. The Navy Yard is a business campus, so check the entrance before going. Chartered June 1, 1959.

records.name: Junior League of Philadelphia
records.summary: A volunteer group for women that takes new members each year through a New Member Program. It holds information sessions before people apply, so you can learn what it is like first.
records.what_you_do: Apply during the yearly new member window and attend the new member program. After joining, members volunteer with the league's projects.

schedule.text: A yearly new member program. The 2026 information sessions were in July and September 2026, in the evening (virtual sessions Sept 3 and Sept 9).

cost.text: Dues were not found in the pages I could read

first_step.how: Fill in the New Member Interest Form to hear about upcoming sessions, or email newmember@jlphiladelphia.org
first_step.basis: Joining needs an application within a yearly window, though information sessions let people learn about the group before applying. A sponsoring member is not required.

records.notes: Written from search excerpts of the group's own pages. The site redirects to philadelphia.jl.org, which returned 403 to my fetches, so the full pages were not read. Verify eligibility, dues and session dates before relying on them. A second contact address is membershipdevelopment@jlphiladelphia.org. Registration for the 2026 to 27 program likely closed in mid-September, which I could not confirm.

records.name: League of Women Voters of Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonpartisan group for voter education and voting rights in Philadelphia. It runs public events, such as an Aug 8, 2026 Day of Action for voting rights, and has hosted panels with city council members.
records.what_you_do: Go to a public event, or ask the league how to help at a voter registration or voter guide project.

schedule.text: The Aug 8, 2026 Day of Action ran from 10 am at Shissler Recreation Center. No regular meeting schedule was found.

first_step.how: Watch for announced public events, and ask the Pennsylvania state league for the local contact, since no local website was found
first_step.basis: Public events are open to anyone, but I could not find a local way to join or a meeting schedule, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: No local website or contact was found. The Philadelphia page cited in an old archive (palwv.org/philadelphia) returns 404. The state league's contact (palwv.org, info at palwv.org) was not used as a local contact. The Aug 8, 2026 date comes from a search excerpt, because the Action Network page itself returned 'not currently available' to my fetch. Older items (candidate debates, voter guides) are not used as evidence of current activity.

records.name: NAACP Philadelphia Branch
records.summary: The Philadelphia branch of the NAACP, a civil rights organization. Its general membership meetings share branch updates and feature guest speakers.
records.what_you_do: Attend a general membership meeting to hear branch updates, or join the branch as a member.

schedule.text: General membership meetings are announced by the branch. The most recent notice found was for Tuesday, June 16, 2026 at 6 pm.

first_step.how: Watch for the next general membership meeting notice, or join through the national NAACP site
first_step.basis: Membership meetings are announced, but I could not confirm the branch's own contact or whether people who are not members can attend.

records.notes: The branch's own website was not found. The June 2026 notice comes from a directory repost, seen only as a search excerpt because the directory page returned 403 to my fetch. A 2021 news report described the branch's membership meetings as closed and online. That is older reporting and is not used for status. The national site's 'Join a local unit' link goes to a membership portal form, which I did not use. Older news from 2020 and 2021 covers branch leadership changes; not recorded here.

records.name: Habitat for Humanity Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that builds and repairs homes with families. Homeowners help build their own homes and then buy them with an affordable mortgage. It also runs a ReStore that sells donated furniture and home goods to fund its work.
records.what_you_do: Help on a build or repair day as an individual or as a group, shop or volunteer at the ReStore, or join the Young Professionals network.

cost.text: Cost to volunteer is not listed on the pages I read

first_step.how: Start on the volunteer page and pick individual or group volunteering, or email volunteer@habitatphiladelphia.org
first_step.basis: Open to everyone with a published volunteer page and email, but the pages I read gave no sign-up steps, age limits or build dates.

records.notes: Two October 2026 items are listed on the homepage: the 2026 Construction Sprint (a fundraising challenge, Oct 20) and Habi Hour (Oct 29). Pope Leo Village, an interfaith build of 26 homes, is named on the volunteer page without dates. The site domain is habitatphiladelphia.org. Other contacts on the contact page are info@habitatphiladelphia.org and restore@habitatphiladelphia.org. The homepage was read through a summary tool, so the event dates should be rechecked.

notes: Budget: all 8 WebSearch calls were used, so searching stopped there. Lions: no Philadelphia club confirmed; the national finder and the Lafayette Hill tax listing were the only leads. Kiwanis: no Philadelphia club confirmed; all Kiwanis pages were blocked (403). Rotary: the national finder returned 429 every time, so the Rotary Club of Philadelphia record comes from its own site (high confidence) and the other Rotary names are leads. Toastmasters: the national finder loads with no list (script only), so each Philadelphia club page was read on its own; five clubs are published, and Phly Phorum, Blue Bell and University City are leads. Optimist: read through the national directory's state and city lists. Two Philadelphia-listed clubs were checked: one is published with status unknown, and Galilee Community is out of area because it meets in Ambler. LWV: no local website found, and the only dated item (Aug 8, 2026) comes from a search excerpt (low confidence). NAACP: no branch website found; the June 2026 notice comes from a directory repost seen through search (low confidence). Junior League: the group's own site redirects to a host that returns 403, so its facts come from search excerpts (low confidence). Habitat: read from habitatphiladelphia.org (the habitatphilly.org domain does not resolve). Other failures: palwv.org/philadelphia 404, optimist.org/find-a-club 404, naacp.org/find-resources/branches 404, and several Philadelphia-named domains did not resolve. The NAACP national 'Join a local unit' link leads to a membership portal form, which was not used. Toastmasters' national finder and the Action Network widget showed no list or no content, so they are not counted as blocked. All summaries and notes were written by hand, with no dashes used as punctuation.
